extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 temporal tasks spanning perception to cognition that cannot be effectively solved using a single frame. It contains 200 multiple-choice question-answer pairs per task, generated from public video datasets and their annotations, with each QA pair corresponding to a distinct video.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.citeAs: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, and Yu Qiao. MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. arXiv:2311.17005v4 [cs.CV], 23 May 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos and existing ground-truth annotations were selected from 11 public video benchmarks. Dataset selection sought diverse domains and scenes, including first-person and third-person perspectives, indoor and outdoor environments, and real-world and simulated videos. Temporal tasks were defined by adapting static image tasks with dynamic goals. Selected annotations were directly adopted or automatically converted into multiple-choice QA, producing 200 pairs for each of 20 tasks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public videos and annotations from STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA. The appendix clarifies that Action Antonym videos come from SthSthV2, while their antonyms come from PAXION.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: STAR video clips were modified by randomly shifting their start or end points to increase event-localization difficulty. Existing annotations were converted into multiple-choice QA where necessary. For all questions, 3 to 5 answer options were randomly sampled from available candidates and their order shuffled. An LLM was used to ensure options had similar and reasonable text lengths.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Short clips with negligible motion and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts were removed; selected videos primarily ranged from 5 to 35 seconds. Task-specific filters selected relevant annotation categories, durations, and events. CLEVRER questions requiring more than 10 descriptive conditions were excluded, with additional task-specific program-length thresholds detailed in Table 19. Moving Direction videos were restricted to objects that were stationary or moving in a single direction. Scene Transition videos required continuous scene labels. State Change questions requiring audio were excluded, and TVQA QA pairs were adopted without subtitles.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Existing multiple-choice QA annotations were directly adopted when available. Otherwise, ChatGPT generated questions based on temporal task definitions; the appendix specifies generating 3 to 5 questions for datasets requiring question generation. Answer candidates were generally constructed from ground-truth annotations using templates, including action antonyms, object attributes, movement directions, temporal locations, and navigation actions. ChatGPT converted FunQA open-ended QA into multiple-choice QA and generated Scene Transition QA from original annotations. Fine-grained Action options were sampled from the top-six predictions of UMT-L/16. The final benchmark contains 200 multiple-choice QA pairs per task.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Final answers are grounded in source-dataset annotations. Multiple-choice QA was chosen instead of open-ended QA to avoid scoring bias from LLM evaluators and the need for user studies. Answer options were randomly sampled and shuffled to improve evaluation robustness. An LLM adjusted option lengths to prevent answer leakage caused by correct answers tending to be longer.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies potential answer leakage when longer answer options tend to be correct and mitigates it by using an LLM to make options similar in length. It also notes source overlap between VideoChat2 instruction-tuning data and MVBench: CLEVRER instruction data contains questions similar to Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference, and Action Antonym videos originate from SthSthV2, which is also used for instruction tuning.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: VideoChat2 evaluation on MVBench is not strictly out-of-domain because its instruction-tuning data overlaps with benchmark sources, particularly CLEVRER and SthSthV2. The paper suggests that visual information alone may be insufficient for complex egocentric navigation and episodic reasoning, and that additional modalities such as depth and audio could be beneficial.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of image and video multi-modal large language models across 20 tasks, including action understanding, object tracking and interaction, localization, scene transitions, counting, attributes, pose, character order, navigation, episodic reasoning, and counterfactual inference. Evaluation uses multiple-choice accuracy. The proposed protocol combines a system prompt emphasizing temporal evolution with the answer prefix 'Best Option: (' to obtain option outputs reliably.
